title: Dedicated capacity throughput: SLA language, error budget math, and contract clauses
creator: Sofia Moreno
description: Define precise throughput guarantees for Dedicated capacity, translate guarantees into measurable SLOs and error budgets, and produce contract language for customer agreements and service credits. This ticket covers measurement windows, failure modes (capacity exhaustion, degraded kernels, network partitions), autoscaling expectations (burst vs guaranteed sustained throughput), and the contractual escalation / credit model.
acceptance_criteria: A clear definition of 'Throughput Guarantee' suitable for contract insertion
Formal error budget calculation with examples for monthly billing cycles
Contract clause draft (legal-ready wording) including service credits, notification obligations, and maintenance exemptions
Implementation checklist for engineering: metrics, dashboards, alerts, and simulation plan
Sign-off from Legal and Engineering on measurement method and credit math

decisions: Measure throughput compliance on 5-minute aligned windows; a window is compliant if observed offered throughput >= contracted throughput target for that window.
Monthly SLO: 99.5% of 5-minute windows in a calendar month must be compliant to meet the Throughput Guarantee.
Error budget: the remainder (0.5%) equals allowed non-compliant minutes. Credits are calculated per 0.5% breach increment with a hard cap at 50% of monthly Dedicated fees.

Autoscaling behavior: Dedicated capacity will support short bursts above guaranteed throughput for up to the customer's declared burst budget; sustained excess request patterns require committed capacity increases.
Measurement point: calculate at the customer pool ingress (post-routing, pre-execution) to ensure consistent attribution and avoid double-counting internal retries.

contract_excerpt: Throughput Guarantee. Redwood Inference guarantees that Dedicated capacity will provide the contracted sustained throughput (measured in tokens/second) to Customer's Reserved Pool. Measurement shall be performed on five-minute aligned windows; a window is deemed compliant when the observed throughput available to the Customer's pool is greater than or equal to the Contracted Throughput. The Monthly Throughput SLO is 99.5% of windows compliant per calendar month. Error Budget and Credits. In the event the Monthly Throughput SLO is not met, Customer will be eligible for service credits calculated as follows: for each 0.5 percentage point below the SLO, Redwood will issue a credit equal to 5% of that month's Dedicated capacity fees, up to a cumulative maximum credit equal to 50% of that month's Dedicated capacity fees. Exclusions. Credits will not apply to outages caused by Customer misconfiguration, third-party dependencies, force majeure, or Scheduled Maintenance (Customer will be notified at least 72 hours in advance). Redwood will notify Customer within 48 hours of detecting a potential SLO breach and provide a remediation plan. The parties agree that service credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for throughput SLA failures.
